newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-Danka in deal with Kodak.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Danka in deal with Kodak.

text.p: Danka Business Systems Plc said it is involved in talks "in connnection with a possible substantial acquisition." It said in the acquisition would not involve the issue of equity and a further announcement, "will follow in due course."
This is the full text of the announcement.
Danka to Create Worldwide Office Imaging Powerhouse with Kodak Deal; Acquires Sales, Service and Facilities Management Operations of Kodak's Office Imaging Business

ST. PETERSBURG, Fla./ROCHESTER, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 9, 1996--Danka Business Systems PLC and Eastman Kodak Company today announced that they have signed an agreement for Danka to acquire the sales, marketing, and equipment service operations of Kodak's Office Imaging business, as well as Kodak's facilities management business known as Kodak Imaging Services. The resulting business will offer global coverage in office products and services with more than 700 offices in 35 countries around the world.

In connection with this agreement, Danka and Kodak will enter into a strategic alliance whereby Kodak will supply high volume copiers and printers to Danka. The agreement will make Danka the principal distributor of Kodak-branded office copiers and printers. Kodak will retain its manufacturing and research and development functions supporting Office Imaging.

Under the terms of the agreement, Danka will pay Kodak $684 million in cash and assume certain assets and operating liabilities to acquire the sales, marketing, and equipment service functions of Kodak's Office Imaging business, as well as Kodak's facilities management business. Kodak will retain $123 million in receivables stemming from long-term copier leases in the U.K. and Canada.

Upon completion of the transaction, Danka's current, annualized sales will be approximately $3.5 billion. Its recurring revenue stream from service, supplies and rentals would more than double to $2 billion.

As of December 31, 1995, the unaudited book value of the net assets to be acquired by Danka was approximately $800 million. In the year ending December 31, 1995, the assets of the business had revenues of $1.8 billion and net earnings before tax of approximately $20 million, reflecting certain corporate expenses.

"This strategic alliance will allow Danka to offer customers a unique combination of unparalleled service and support with global coverage, as well as a wide choice in equipment - from small copiers to high- volume duplicators, fax machines and state-of-the art digital copiers/printers," said Dan Doyle, Chief Executive Officer of Danka Business Systems PLC. "We will be the single-source solution for all office imaging needs. We are excited about the opportunity to create a single, focused organization. The acquisition of Kodak's sales, service and facilities management business will bring together the mutual expertise and track records of our fine organizations."

Commenting on the agreement, Kodak's Assistant Chief Operating Officer, Carl F. Kohrt, said, "We are delighted to form this strategic alliance with Danka as the critical element in repositioning our Office Imaging business. We are also pleased that the sale of the business successfully achieves our objectives of strengthening the business and maximizing its value to Kodak while simultaneously looking out for the interests of our customers and our people."

"This alliance promises to increase access to the market for Kodak-branded office imaging products," Kohrt added. "In addition, Danka's acquisition of our sales, marketing, and facilities management operations will place our sales and service people in a growing organization that is devoted exclusively to providing solutions for the office."

Kodak's research and development efforts for electrophotography will provide a pipeline of new black and white and accent color office imaging products for Danka to market. This effort will be stronger and more focused as the two companies will work together to identify product solutions to customer needs. In addition, Kodak will retain its key color electrophotography technology for use in Kodak's other imaging businesses.

This effort will be stronger and more focused as the two companies will work together to identify product solutions to customer needs. Danka stated that the transaction would be funded exclusively with bank debt under a six-year, $1.2 billion fully underwritten commitment. This commitment will be used to refinance Danka's existing debt and revolving credit facilities as well as to acquire Kodak's related sales, service and facilities management assets. Danka expects to take a one-time restructuring charge of $25 million to $35 million in its third fiscal quarter (fourth quarter calendar) related to the integration of the acquired Kodak operations with Danka's existing service and sales network. Danka also stated that it expects the acquisition to be accretive to earnings in the first twelve months of operations.

Danka also announced that Peter Meier, currently regional business general manager of Office Imaging for EAMER (Kodak's Europe, Africa, Middle East Region), will manage the acquired sales and service business worldwide when the transaction is completed. "EAMER's significantly improved performance in the past two years is due in large measure to Peter's management skills, energy and vision for the region," stated Doyle. "He will play a key role in bringing Office Imaging as a whole up to its full potential." Meier will relocate to Rochester, NY, for this new assignment.
Danka noted that their facilities management business will be managed separately from the acquired sales and service operations.

Over the past year, Kodak has completely reformatted its equipment manufacturing workflow, and improved cycle time of engineering for the development and production of copiers and printers, a process that has already resulted in significant cost reductions and manufacturing efficiencies. Kodak will build on this foundation as it drives for continuous improvement and productivity gains to ensure a continuous flow of high-quality products in a cost-efficient manner.
Approximately 10,400 Kodak employees supporting the business worldwide will be offered employment by Danka. About 6,000 are located in the U.S.

Kohrt praised the Kodak people who support this business, pointing out that they bring a proven track record to Danka. "Kodak copiers have been consistently ranked tops in terms of image quality and customer satisfaction. This recognition has been earned by the many people supporting the Office Imaging, Customer Equipment Service, and Kodak Imaging Services business," he said.
Completion of the agreement is subject to approval by Danka shareholders as well as regulatory consents. The parties plan to close the transaction by the end of 1996.

Danka Business Systems PLC, headquartered in St. Petersburg, Florida, is one of the largest and fastest growing independent suppliers of automated office equipment and related service and supplies in North America, Europe, Australia and New Zealand. Danka's revenues have grown at a compounded rate of more than 40 percent in the last five years. On completion of the transaction, Danka will employ 22,000 people and have more than 700 offices in 35 countries around the world. Danka's ADSs are listed on the NASDAQ and its Ordinary shares are listed on the London Stock Exchange.
